shared_elements: frontal human face with eyes, nose and mouth
arms indicated at the sides of the body
rounded boss/disc on the chest area
row of small repeated marks (teeth-like / incised band)
justification: Both are upright grey stone anthropomorphic monoliths presenting a frontal face above a torso with arms folded or laid across a chest bearing a raised circular boss, and both include a band of small repeated incisions. The decisive difference is technique and mass: A is a flat slab covered with shallow, linear low-relief that reads almost as drawing, while B is a fully three-dimensional, deeply modelled carving with stacked heads and pronounced volumetric features.
